label: glycolic acid
nothermo: the ionisation (pK, dH) of glycolic acid is printed in Miller & Smith-Magowan Table 6, so the SPECIATION is complete.  Its formation data are NOT entered: Miller Table 5 (p. 1056) prints dHf(cr) -664.0, dH(soln) +15.94 and dHf(aq acid) -651.0, which do not close (-664.0 + 15.94 = -648.06, 2.9 kJ/mol from the printed aqueous value, the row marked error estimated); the NBS tables print glycolate -652.3 (dHf only, no entropy).  Three readings disagree by 4.7 kJ/mol and the work in hand does not say which is right, so the energy route through glycolate REFUSES BY NAME.
note: Glycolic acid is not in Goldberg, Kishore & Lennen (2002); Miller & Smith-Magowan take its pK and dH_ion from Christensen & Hansen (their ref. 77CHR/HAN).

label: arsenic acid
note: dCp is not printed for arsenic acid.  The existing species H2AsO4 and HAsO4 carry NBS formation data (C320) and the new records are written from the neutral master H3AsO4.

label: pyrophosphoric acid
note: The catalogue family is `phosphate`; pyrophosphate joins it for navigation.

label: sulfurous acid
note: Goldberg writes the neutral acid H2SO3; the species H2SO3 is the formal stoichiometric acid (aqueous SO2).

label: hydrazine
note: The neutral base is `Hydrazine`, not `N2H4`: the catalogue holds a component N2H4, a derived neutral species of that name would have to carry the `aq` suffix, and check_species_identity pins that suffix as a closed historical class (so `N2H4aq` is refused).  The records are written from the diprotonated master N2H6.
